centralMetadataChanges.proposal: Describe as browser DNS lookup/timing, not ICMP ping or proof that a host is reachable. Consider renaming the display title to DNS Response Check.
Describe a selected historical reference through December 2024 and link the official live history; remove real-time tracking claims.
Remove numeric SEO grades, ranking predictions and universal optimal-length guarantees. Describe actual parsing/counting checks.
State static HTML checks only; no WCAG certification, rendered contrast or runtime keyboard/focus audit.
State local phrase templates/frequency extraction; no search volume, competition, semantic AI or live suggestions.
State Google-provider favicon bytes may be generic fallback; PNG/ICO only, max 20 domains, no invented site-discovery guarantee.
State browser HEAD/CORS limits and Unknown results, max 20 URLs. Do not claim full-site crawling.
Public RDAP registration age, not website age; registry/CORS/data-availability restrictions apply.
Describe paste modes plus CORS-enabled direct URL reads. No unrestricted proxy crawling or execution of page scripts.
Locally administered unicast test addresses from Web Crypto; no vendor assignments or global uniqueness guarantee.

coordinatorFollowups.finding: Existing shared endpoint uses weak substring origin checks, incomplete private-host checks, follows redirects, clears timeout before unbounded body read. Owned clients now use direct bounded CORS reads instead; parent should separately review/repair the shared endpoint.
Client bounds/decodes returned bytes, but existing shared server endpoint still buffers upstream bytes without a size cap or downstream cancellation. Parent owns server hardening.
Existing shared server resolver does not allow NS and buffers JSON. Owned clients query bounded Google DoH directly to preserve NS and distinct resolver errors.
